under_documentation_gap: New or acute dependence in activities of daily living is present but not captured as an objective finding tied to medical necessity (why safe care cannot be delivered at a lower level).
predicts: New ADL dependence is independently associated with higher admission likelihood and with prolonged stay and need for post-acute coordination; it is a documentable functional finding, not a status lever.
independently_indicated_actions: Physical/occupational therapy functional and safe-discharge assessment

citations.source: JAMA Internal Medicine (Smulowitz et al., functional status, cognition, social support and ED admission)
JAMA (Studenski et al., gait speed and survival in older adults)

under_documentation_gap: A Clinical Frailty Scale finding (moderate-to-severe frailty) is present in the record but not documented as an objective finding supporting the expected hospital course.
predicts: Higher Clinical Frailty Scale grades are associated, in a graded fashion, with increased mortality, prolonged length of stay, failed discharge, and post-acute care need; the score documents existing risk and does not by itself qualify a status.

citations.source: CMAJ (Rockwood et al., a global clinical measure of fitness and frailty in elderly people)
Annals of Emergency Medicine (Kaeppeli et al., Clinical Frailty Scale and 30-day mortality in ED older adults)

under_documentation_gap: Cognitive impairment or delirium risk is present but not documented as affecting the ability to self-manage therapy or to be safely cared for at a lower level.
predicts: Cognitive impairment is independently associated with higher admission likelihood and elevated delirium risk requiring monitoring; it is a documentable finding, not a status lever.
independently_indicated_actions: Documented cognitive screen and capacity assessment

under_documentation_gap: A recent-hospitalization / high-readmission-risk history is present but not documented as part of the expected hospital course and care-coordination need.
predicts: Recent hospitalizations are associated with higher readmission risk and can support the physician's reasonable expectation of a medically necessary multi-midnight course when active care is still required; it is a documentation and expectation hook, not a status lever.

citations.source: CMS Two-Midnight Rule (42 CFR 412.3; reasonable expectation of medically necessary care)
citations.locator: expectation based on complexity and recovery time

citations.source: CMS SNF three-day inpatient rule (42 CFR 409.30; patient-protection stake of accurate status)

under_documentation_gap: Absent caregiver support or unsafe home context is present, but it is NOT documented as preventing safe delivery of otherwise-needed medical care at a lower level. Social risk supports inpatient ONLY when it makes safe delivery of needed medical care impossible at a lower level; pure placement/disposition delay does not.
predicts: Available social support lowers admission likelihood; its absence is a documentable risk but, on its own, does not establish medical necessity unless it prevents safe delivery of needed medical care.
independently_indicated_actions: Social-work assessment linking the social barrier to a specific medical-care-delivery failure

citations.source: JAMA Internal Medicine (Smulowitz et al., social support and ED admission)
